subject: MAP: decongestion plan and staggered acceptance protocol for close
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@apexhealth.com>, Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@apexhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com, camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: decongestion plan and staggered acceptance protocol for close

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the productive demo yesterday. Per our call, I took a pass on the Mutual Action Plan to reduce the single-day pressure on procurement and cutover. Attached is MAP_v2.xlsx — the high-level changes are:  

- Staggered acceptance windows (pilot -> phased go-live) so you can accept core functionality first and defer lower-risk integrations to week+1.
- A two-week surge buffer we can reserve in Dedicated to avoid capacity-driven timeouts during the final verification run.
- Conditionally applied credit for execution slippage if procurement pushes past the committed runway (see Pricing_Adjustment.csv we can share if needed).

Risks we flagged:
- Procurement freeze (known internal constraint) — will require procurement point-of-contact to sign timelines.
- SOC2 evidence request: we can surface the relevant artifacts but will need the security questionnaire completed by Friday to keep the current close target.
- Cutover smoke test: we recommend a canary run 48 hours before the pilot acceptance window.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm target approval date and whether the 2-week buffer is acceptable? (cc'ing procurement if helpful)
2) Elena/Tom: confirm which downstream integrations you want in pilot vs phased acceptance (I highlighted suggested items in MAP_v2).
3) If procurement expects a longer freeze, propose an alternate acceptance date and we'll provide a rebaseline proposal with explicit tradeoffs (cost, SLA, sequencing).

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx, SOC2_Summary.pdf

Best,
Mina Haddad
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

--
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@apexhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@apexhealth.com>, procurement@apexhealth.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: decongestion plan and staggered acceptance protocol for close

Mina —

Thanks for the updated MAP (appreciate the clarity). Quick notes from procurement / program: 

- We have a procurement hold window the week of 29 Jun for org-level budget reviews. Likely outcome: approvals push 10–14 days.
- Procurement will not sign any PLA until the SOC2 evidence is reviewed by our security team — sharing procurement_timeline.xlsx with their internal dates.

We like the staggered acceptance approach — that helps keep the core platform live while integrations are sequenced. Two asks from our side: 
1) Can Redwood commit to a 48-hour canary and a rollback plan with clear SLAs for the pilot?
2) If we need to slide the close by two weeks, can you provide a short cost impact summary and any credits for the delay?

cc: procurement@apexhealth.com for timeline visibility.

Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Integrations, Apex Health
elena.soto@apexhealth.com

Subject: Re: MAP: decongestion plan and staggered acceptance protocol for close

Elena / Mina —

Appreciate the pragmatic approach. Quick operational suggestions from the infra side that should reduce slippage risk: 

- Dedicated surge buffer: we can reserve a small Dedicated pool for your pilot and hold capacity for the 48-hour canary window. This prevents noisy neighbor issues during final verification.
- Canary runbook: attached CanaryRun_Playbook.pdf —  tasks, success criteria, rollback steps. We will own the run execution with your SREs.
- Conditional closing credit: we can offer a one-time execution credit (cap at US$25,000) if procurement-dependent delays push final acceptance past the agreed rebaseline window. Pricing_Adjustment.csv shows the expected unit cost with and without the buffer.

If procurement confirms a ~10–14 day slide, we propose the following stitch plan: 
A) Keep pilot acceptance date = original target + 14 days;
B) Schedule canary at T-2 days;
C) Reserve Dedicated surge capacity for T-2 through T+3 days;
D) Apply conditional credit if procurement delay is confirmed in writing and extends beyond the agreed buffer.

I will draft the change paragraph for the MAP and circulate for signatures once procurement confirms.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Solutions, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwoodinference.com

Team —

Summary / escalation note (internal + external visibility):

1) Procurement has a planned freeze the week of 29 Jun that is likely to push approvals by ~10–14 days. That creates a risk of close-date slippage for APX-4821.

2) Mitigations agreed:
   - Staggered acceptance windows (pilot first, phased acceptance after) to keep core product live.
   - Redwood will run a 48-hour canary and reserves Dedicated surge capacity for the T-2 through T+3 window if procurement confirms the slide.
   - Conditional one-time execution credit up to $25,000 if procurement delay is documented and extends past the agreed buffer.

3) Asks of Leadership (cc: Camila, Lauren):
   - Approve the conditional $25k execution credit and the SLA exception for the T-2 canary window. This is a one-off for APX-4821 to de-risk a high-value account.
   - If approved, I will update MAP_v2 and send the revised paragraph to procurement for sign-off.

4) External actions 
   - Elena / Tom: please confirm whether you want the following integrations in pilot vs phase 2 by EOD Thu so we can lock the cutover checklist.
   - Procurement: please share confirmation of the approval date in writing so we can trigger the Dedicated reservation and credit clause.

If leadership approves, I will: (a) update the MAP appendix with the surge/reservation terms, (b) attach the canary playbook to the MAP, and (c) update HubSpot with the agreed rebaseline and credit terms.

Thanks — we want to avoid a hard stop on the close and keep momentum.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference
